Hi all,

Thanks again for your time this week — excited to run a short (45m) technical walkthrough of our inference runtime next week so we can cover performance/latency examples for your cross-region workloads.

Important note: US daylight saving starts on Sun, Mar 9, while EU/JP don't switch at the same time. That means a slot that looks stable when scheduled in ET will shift for EU participants the following week. To avoid confusion, could you confirm which of these windows works for each office (I listed local times for clarity):

Option A — Tue, Mar 11
- 10:00 ET / 15:00 CET / 00:00 JST (Wed)

Option B — Wed, Mar 12
- 14:00 ET / 19:00 CET / 03:00 JST (Thu) — later for APAC

If neither works, I can propose a morning-UTC-centered slot (13:00 UTC) that tends to be friendlier for US/EU/APAC balance.

Agenda draft attached; expecting customers to share sample request volumes so we can demo relevant batching/latency behavior.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Rishi@redwood.ai

Bonjour Rishi — thanks for the options. A quick clarification: in Paris we are CET (UTC+1) for the moment and will not advance until the end of the month, so the local wall-clock for Option A is 15:00 CET (good), Option B at 19:00 CET is also ok but a bit late for our ops team.

One concern: you mentioned US DST starts this weekend (I see that). Could you please confirm that the calendar invite will show local times correctly for each participant? We had one previous meeting where the invite read differently in Gmail vs Outlook.

Prefer Option A (Mar 11 at 15:00 CET) if APAC can tolerate the midnight JST time — otherwise we should pick your 13:00 UTC suggestion.

Merci,
Aline

- Option B shifts EU late into their evening.
